newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania OTC closes firmer on volatile trading.
newsitem.headline: Romania OTC closes firmer on volatile trading.

text.p: Romania's over-the-counter market (OTC) ended firmer on Thursday in volatile trading boosted in part by the government's approval of portfolio investment rules, traders said.
One small-cap stock, a River Danube port operator, underwent dramatic swings as one buyer paid several hundred times the previous closing price to acquire a large stake.
Operators forecast a slightly bullish mood for Friday's session and expected the recovery to be maintained.
On Thursday 129 stocks prices rose, 84 were down, while 274 remained flat.
Traders said foreign investors were pleased with the new rules on portfolio investments, but were awaiting more details.
"Our foreign clients said it was a good step for the local capital market, but they want more tehnical information on portfolio investments in Romania," one trader said.
Romania's government approved on Wednesday a decree that establishes for the first time clear rules on capital gains, setting tax on gains repatriation at four percent.

Unofficial indices VAB-RA, computed by Vanguard securities and BIG-OTC, compiled by the BIG brokerage house, rose to 3,550.4 and 2,576.34 points, respectively, gaining 3.6 percent and 4.45 percent. Both indices are computed based on average prices of OTC listings.

Operators said that, even though prices were volatile throughout the session, they saw a strong buying drive from investors. River Danube port operator Port Docuri Galati traded 65,000 shares at 60,100 lei each in a single mid-day transaction. But it later closed at 3,500, unchanged from its previous close.
Some cement makers and oil refineries continued to stay in the investors' focus, but underwent no major movements.
Cement makers Romcim and Moldocim closed flat at 69,000 lei and 28,500, respectively, while oil refineries Petrobrazi and Arpechim firmed 3,000 lei and 650 to close at 21,500 lei and 26,250.
Thursday's turnover rose to 15.8 billion lei from 7.3 billion on Wednesday, with 3.2 million shares traded.
The VAB-RA index is displayed on VANGUARD.
